$comment: Declarative set of perch infra contracts that are published + content-addressed deployed (deploy_stateless, salt = wasm_hash) via the managed `stateless` registry. Consumed by scripts/bootstrap-testnet.sh (PERCH_STATELESS=1) and, once #41 lands, by the registry_contract! resolver macro + perch-compile's interpreter_wasm_hash. Requires #38 (upstream StatelessDeployable / deploy-stateless CLI) and #39 (crates/perch-stateless-registry). perch-account is deliberately ABSENT: its __constructor takes admin_signers, so it is not content-addressable and stays name-salted on unverified/perch.

registry.name: stateless
registry.note: A second managed subregistry, registered as `stateless` under unverified/perch (admin=manager=deployer at deploy, manager rotated to the perch smart account in phase 6). Its deploy_stateless entry point uses salt = wasm_hash. Built by #39; the entry point is #38's StatelessDeployable.

contracts.name: perch-ed25519-verifier
contracts.note: Holds no storage. Pure ed25519 signature verification — one shared, content-addressed instance is safe for every account.

contracts.name: perch-doc-compiler
contracts.note: Holds no storage. compile_doc parses + validates + compiles PolicyDoc JSON on-chain; shared by every account (accounts carry no parser).

contracts.name: perch-interpreter
contracts.author: @SMART_ACCOUNT@
contracts.note: Stateful, but every slot is keyed by DataKey::Program(smart_account, context_rule_id) (crates/perch-interpreter/src/lib.rs). Each (account, rule) owns an isolated program slot with no cross-account key, so one shared content-addressed singleton is multi-tenant-safe. Published with --author = the perch smart account: the registry has no author transfer, so this fixes republish auth to the smart account forever (see phase 3).
